title: Valuation criterion for closedness of the image of a quasi-compact immersion
statement: Let j:Z\to S be a quasi-compact immersion of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Assume that for every valuation ring A with fraction field K, every morphism g:Spec(A)\to S whose restriction Spec(K)\to S factors through j also factors through j. Then the image j(Z) is closed in S. In particular, a quasi-compact immersion with this valuative specialization property is a closed immersion.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image, Tag 02JQ, and Lemma morphisms-lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, Tag 01R8

proof.text: Let s be any point of the closure of the range of j. The valuation-probe statement [lem-sc-picard-valuation-probe-closure] supplies a valuation ring A with fraction field K, a map g:Spec(A)→S whose closed point maps to s, and a generic map Spec(K)→Z whose composite with j is the restriction of g.
By the assumed valuative property, g factors through j. Therefore its closed point s lies in the range of j. Since every point of the closure of the range lies in the range, the range j(Z) is closed.
Since j is an immersion with closed image j(Z), the criterion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] (Tag 01IQ) shows that j is a closed immersion.
